sanskrit: yad yac ca kurute karma śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham pūrvadehakṛtaṃ sarvam avaśyam upabhujyate
english: Whatever deed one performs, whether good or evil, all that was done in a former body must of necessity be enjoyed as its fruit.

sanskrit: tatas tat kṣīyate caiva punaś cānyat pracīyate yāvat tan mokṣayogasthaṃ dharmaṃ naivāvabudhyate
english: Then that karma is worn away, and yet again another is heaped up, so long as one does not come to understand the dharma that rests upon the discipline of liberation.

sanskrit: tatra dharmaṃ pravakṣyāmi sukhī bhavati yena vai āvartamāno jātīṣu tathānyonyāsu sattama
english: On this I shall now declare the dharma by which one becomes happy, O most excellent, even while revolving through births, one after another.

sanskrit: dānaṃ vrataṃ brahmacaryaṃ yathoktavratadhāraṇam damaḥ praśāntatā caiva bhūtānāṃ cānukampanam
english: Giving, observance of vows, chastity, the keeping of vows as enjoined, self-restraint, tranquillity, and compassion toward living beings;

sanskrit: saṃyamaś cānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca parasvādānavarjanam vyalīkānām akaraṇaṃ bhūtānāṃ yatra sā bhuvi
english: control of the senses and absence of cruelty, refraining from seizing what belongs to another, the doing of no harm to living beings—where this exists upon the earth;

sanskrit: mātāpitroś ca śuśrūṣā devatātithipūjanam gurupūjā ghṛṇā śaucaṃ nityam indriyasaṃyamaḥ
english: service to mother and father, honoring of the gods and guests, reverence for the teacher, tenderness, purity, and constant restraint of the senses;

sanskrit: pravartanaṃ śubhānāṃ ca tat satāṃ vṛttam ucyate tato dharmaḥ prabhavati yaḥ prajāḥ pāti śāśvatīḥ
english: and the setting in motion of all that is auspicious—this is called the conduct of the good. From it springs forth the dharma that protects creatures everlastingly.

sanskrit: evaṃ satsu sadā paśyet tatra hy eṣā dhruvā sthitiḥ ācāro dharmam ācaṣṭe yasmin santo vyavasthitāḥ
english: Thus one should ever look upon the good, for in them is this firm foundation. Conduct reveals the dharma, that wherein the good are established.

sanskrit: teṣu tad dharmanikṣiptaṃ yaḥ sa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ yas taṃ samabhipadyeta na sa durgatim āpnuyāt
english: In them is this dharma laid up as a deposit, and it is the eternal dharma. Whoever attains to it shall not come to an evil destiny.

sanskrit: ato niyamyate lokaḥ pramuhya dharmavartmasu yas tu yogī ca muktaś ca sa etebhyo viśiṣyate
english: By this the world is governed, even when bewildered upon the paths of dharma. But he who is a yogin and one who is freed surpasses all of these.

sanskrit: vartamānasya dharmeṇa puruṣasya yathā tathā saṃsāratāraṇaṃ hy asya kālena mahatā bhavet
english: For the man who conducts himself according to dharma, in whatever measure, the crossing over of the round of rebirth comes to pass, though only after a great length of time.

sanskrit: evaṃ pūrvakṛtaṃ karma sarvo jantur niṣevate sarvaṃ tat kāraṇaṃ yena nikṛto 'yam ihāgataḥ
english: Thus every creature partakes of the karma done before; all that is the cause whereby, cast down, it has come hither into this world.

sanskrit: śarīragrahaṇaṃ cāsya kena pūrvaṃ prakalpitam ity evaṃ saṃśayo loke tac ca vakṣyāmy ataḥ param
english: And by whom was the taking on of a body first ordained for it?—such is the doubt that arises in the world; that too I shall declare hereafter.

sanskrit: śarīram ātmanaḥ kṛtvā sarvabhūtapitāmahaḥ trailokyam asṛjad brahmā kṛtsnaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam
english: Having made a body for himself, Brahmā, the grandsire of all beings, created the three worlds entire, with all that moves and stands still.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradhānam asṛjac cetanā sā śarīriṇām yayā sarvam idaṃ vyāptaṃ yāṃ loke paramāṃ viduḥ
english: Then he created Pradhāna, that consciousness of embodied beings, by which all this is pervaded, and which in the world they know as supreme.

sanskrit: iha tat kṣaram ity uktaṃ paraṃ tv amṛtam akṣaram trayāṇāṃ mithunaṃ sarvam ekaikasya pṛthak pṛthak
english: Here that is called the perishable, but the supreme is the immortal and imperishable. Of the three there is a coupling, and yet each one stands apart, severally.

sanskrit: asṛjat sarvabhūtāni pūrvasṛṣṭaḥ prajāpatiḥ sthāvarāṇi ca bhūtāni ity eṣā paurvikī śrutiḥ
english: Prajāpati, himself first created, created all living beings and the things that stand fixed—such is the ancient sacred lore.

sanskrit: tasya kālaparīmāṇam akarot sa pitāmahaḥ bhūteṣu parivṛttiṃ ca punarāvṛttim eva ca
english: For him the grandsire fixed the measure of time, and among beings their revolving and their returning again and again.

sanskrit: yathātra kaś cin medhāvī dṛṣṭātmā pūrvajanmani yat pravakṣyāmi tat sarvaṃ yathāvad upapadyate
english: As here some wise man, who has beheld the self in a former birth—all that I am about to declare comes to pass for him exactly as I say.

sanskrit: sukhaduḥkhe sadā samyag anitye yaḥ prapaśyati kāyaṃ cāmedhyasaṃghātaṃ vināśaṃ karmasaṃhitam
english: He who ever rightly perceives pleasure and pain as impermanent, and the body as a heap of impurity, doomed to destruction and bound up with karma—

sanskrit: yac ca kiṃ cit sukhaṃ tac ca sarvaṃ duḥkham iti smaran saṃsārasāgaraṃ ghoraṃ tariṣyati sudustaram
english: and who, remembering that whatever pleasure there is, all of it is pain, shall cross over the dreadful ocean of saṃsāra, hard indeed to cross.

sanskrit: jātīmaraṇarogaiś ca samāviṣṭaḥ pradhānavit cetanāvatsu caitanyaṃ samaṃ bhūteṣu paśyati
english: Beset by birth, death, and disease, the knower of Pradhāna beholds in all sentient beings their consciousness as the same.

sanskrit: nirvidyate tataḥ kṛtsnaṃ mārgamāṇaḥ paraṃ padam tasyopadeśaṃ vakṣyāmi yāthātathyena sattama
english: Then he turns away in disgust from the whole of it, seeking the supreme state. Of that I shall give you the teaching truly, O most excellent.

sanskrit: śāśvatasyāvyayasyātha padasya jñānam uttamam procyamānaṃ mayā vipra nibodhedam aśeṣataḥ
english: Now the supreme knowledge of that eternal, undecaying state, as it is declared by me, O brāhmaṇa—mark it well, in its entirety.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca yaḥ syād ekāyane līnas tūṣṇīṃ kiṃ cid acintayan pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ parityajya sa nirārambhako bhavet
english: The brāhmaṇa said: He who is absorbed in the one goal, silent, thinking on nothing, abandoning each former object one by one, becomes free from all undertaking.

sanskrit: sarvamitraḥ sarvasahaḥ samarakto jitendriyaḥ vyapetabhayamanyuś ca kāmahā mucyate naraḥ
english: Friend to all, enduring all, equal-tempered, his senses conquered, with fear and wrath gone from him, the man who has slain desire is set free.

sanskrit: ātmavat sarvabhūteṣu yaś caren niyataḥ śuciḥ amānī nirabhīmānaḥ sarvato mukta eva saḥ
english: He who, restrained and pure, conducts himself toward all beings as toward himself, free of pride and of self-conceit, is wholly liberated.

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ cobhe sukhaduḥkhe tathaiva ca lābhālābhe priyadveṣye yaḥ samaḥ sa ca mucyate
english: He who is the same toward both life and death, toward pleasure and pain alike, toward gain and loss, toward the loved and the hated—he too is set free.

sanskrit: na kasya cit spṛhayate nāvajānāti kiṃ cana nirdvaṃdvo vītarāgātmā sarvato mukta eva saḥ
english: He who longs for nothing whatever, who despises nothing at all, free from the pairs of opposites, his self purged of passion, is wholly liberated.

sanskrit: anamitro 'tha nirbandhur anapatyaś ca yaḥ kva cit tyaktadharmārthakāmaś ca nirākāṅkṣī sa mucyate
english: He who is without an enemy, without a kinsman, and without offspring anywhere, who has renounced dharma, wealth, and desire, and is free of all craving, is set free.

sanskrit: naiva dharmī na cādharmī pūrvopacitahā ca yaḥ dhātukṣayapraśāntātmā nirdvaṃdvaḥ sa vimucyate
english: He who is neither virtuous nor sinful, who destroys what was heaped up before, whose self is stilled by the wasting away of the bodily elements, free of the pairs of opposites, is wholly released.

sanskrit: akarmā cāvikāṅkṣaś ca paśyañ jagad aśāśvatam asvastham avaśaṃ nityaṃ janmasaṃsāramohitam
english: Free of action and free of longing, beholding the world as impermanent, unwell, ever without mastery of itself, bewildered by the round of birth—

sanskrit: vairāgyabuddhiḥ satataṃ tāpadoṣavyapekṣakaḥ ātmabandhavinirmokṣaṃ sa karoty acirād iva
english: his mind ever set on dispassion, mindful of the fault that is suffering, he accomplishes the release of the self from bondage before long.

sanskrit: agandharasam asparśam aśabdam aparigraham arūpam anabhijñeyaṃ dṛṣṭvātmānaṃ vimucyate
english: Beholding the self as without smell, taste, touch, or sound, beyond possession, without form, and not to be known by the senses, he is liberated.

sanskrit: pañcabhūtaguṇair hīnam amūrtimad alepakam aguṇaṃ guṇabhoktāraṃ yaḥ paśyati sa mucyate
english: He who beholds it as devoid of the qualities of the five elements, formless and untainted, itself without qualities yet the enjoyer of qualities—he is set free.

sanskrit: vihāya sarvasaṃkalpān buddhyā śārīramānasān śanair nirvāṇam āpnoti nirindhana ivānalaḥ
english: Casting off by the intellect all imaginings, both of body and of mind, he gradually attains extinction, like a fire that is without fuel.

sanskrit: vimuktaḥ sarvasaṃskārais tato brahma sanātanam param āpnoti saṃśāntam acalaṃ divyam akṣaram
english: Released from all formations, he then attains the eternal Brahman, the supreme—wholly at peace, unmoving, divine, and imperishable.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yogaśāstram anuttamam yaj jñātvā siddham ātmānaṃ loke paśyanti yoginaḥ
english: Beyond this I shall now declare the unsurpassed teaching of yoga, knowing which the yogins behold the self perfected within the world.

sanskrit: tasyopadeśaṃ paśyāmi yathāvat tan nibodha me yair dvāraiś cārayan nityaṃ paśyaty ātmānam ātmani
english: That teaching I perceive aright; mark it from me—the gates through which one, ever roaming, beholds the self within the self.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi tu saṃhṛtya mana ātmani dhārayet tīvraṃ taptvā tapaḥ pūrvaṃ tato yoktum upakramet
english: Withdrawing the senses, one should hold the mind upon the self; having first practiced fierce austerity, one should then set about the yoking.

sanskrit: tapasvī tyaktasaṃkalpo dambhāhaṃkāravarjitaḥ manīṣī manasā vipraḥ paśyaty ātmānam ātmani
english: The ascetic, having abandoned imaginings, free of deceit and of egotism, the wise brāhmaṇa beholds with the mind the self within the self.

sanskrit: sa cec chaknoty ayaṃ sādhur yoktum ātmānam ātmani tata ekāntaśīlaḥ sa paśyaty ātmānam ātmani
english: If this holy man is able to yoke the self within the self, then, devoted to solitude, he beholds the self within the self.

sanskrit: saṃyataḥ satataṃ yukta ātmavān vijitendriyaḥ tathāyam ātmanātmānaṃ sādhu yuktaḥ prapaśyati
english: Restrained, ever disciplined, self-possessed, his senses conquered, thus, well yoked, he beholds the self through the self.

sanskrit: yathā hi puruṣaḥ svapne dṛṣṭvā paśyaty asāv iti tathārūpam ivātmānaṃ sādhu yuktaḥ prapaśyati
english: For just as a man in a dream, having seen, perceives 'that is he,' so the man well yoked beholds the self as if it had taken on a form.

sanskrit: iṣīkāṃ vā yathā muñjāt kaś cin nirhṛtya darśayet yogī niṣkṛṣṭam ātmānaṃ tathā saṃpaśyate tanau
english: And as one might draw forth the reed-stalk from the muñja grass and display it, so the yogin perceives the self drawn forth from within the body.

sanskrit: muñjaṃ śarīraṃ tasyāhur iṣīkām ātmani śritām etan nidarśanaṃ proktaṃ yogavidbhir anuttamam
english: The body they call the muñja, and the self that rests within it the reed: this is the unsurpassed illustration proclaimed by those who know yoga.

sanskrit: yadā hi yuktam ātmānaṃ samyak paśyati dehabhṛt tadāsya neśate kaś cit trailokyasyāpi yaḥ prabhuḥ
english: For when the embodied one rightly beholds the self well yoked, then no one rules over him, not even the lord of the three worlds.

sanskrit: anyonyāś caiva tanavo yatheṣṭaṃ pratipadyate vinivṛtya jarāmṛtyū na hṛṣyati na śocati
english: He takes on at will body after body, one after another; having turned back old age and death, he neither rejoices nor grieves.

sanskrit: devānām api devatvaṃ yuktaḥ kārayate vaśī brahma cāvyayam āpnoti hitvā deham aśāśvatam
english: The yoked one, having mastery, makes even the gods exercise their godhood; and abandoning the impermanent body, he attains the undecaying Brahman.

sanskrit: vinaśyatsv api lokeṣu na bhayaṃ tasya jāyate kliśyamāneṣu bhūteṣu na sa kliśyati kena cit
english: Even when the worlds are perishing, no fear arises in him; though beings are tormented, he is tormented by nothing whatever.

sanskrit: duḥkhaśokamayair ghoraiḥ saṅgasnehasamudbhavaiḥ na vicālyeta yuktātmā niḥspṛhaḥ śāntamānasaḥ
english: By the dreadful agitations made of grief and sorrow, born of attachment and affection, the disciplined self is not shaken—free of longing, his mind at peace.

sanskrit: nainaṃ śastrāṇi vidhyante na mṛtyuś cāsya vidyate nātaḥ sukhataraṃ kiṃ cil loke kva cana vidyate
english: Weapons do not pierce him, nor does death exist for him; than this there is nothing happier to be found anywhere in the world.

sanskrit: samyag yuktvā yadātmānam ātmany eva prapaśyati tadaiva na spṛhayate sākṣād api śatakratoḥ
english: When, having rightly yoked the self, he beholds it within the self alone, then he no longer longs even for the station of Indra himself, lord of the hundred sacrifices.

sanskrit: nirvedas tu na gantavyo yuñjānena kathaṃ cana yogam ekāntaśīlas tu yathā yuñjīta tac chṛṇu
english: But weariness must in no wise be allowed to one who is practicing yoga. Hear now how the man devoted to solitude should join himself to yoga.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭapūrvāṃ diśaṃ cintya yasmin saṃnivaset pure purasyābhyantare tasya manaś cāryaṃ na bāhyataḥ
english: Calling to mind the quarter he has seen before, in whatever city he dwells, within that city his mind is to be set roaming, not outside it.

sanskrit: purasyābhyantare tiṣṭhan yasminn āvasathe vaset tasminn āvasathe dhāryaṃ sabāhyābhyantaraṃ manaḥ
english: Abiding within that city, in whatever dwelling he lodges, in that dwelling the mind, together with its outer and inner parts, is to be held fast.

sanskrit: pracintyāvasathaṃ kṛtsnaṃ yasmin kāye 'vatiṣṭhate tasmin kāye manaś cāryaṃ na kathaṃ cana bāhyataḥ
english: Having contemplated the whole dwelling, in whatever body he abides, in that body the mind is to be made to roam, in no wise outside it.

sanskrit: saṃniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ nirghoṣe nirjane vane kāyam abhyantaraṃ kṛtsnam ekāgraḥ paricintayet
english: Curbing the host of the senses, in a forest soundless and unpeopled, one should with single-minded focus contemplate the whole body within.

sanskrit: dantāṃs tālu ca jihvāṃ ca galaṃ grīvāṃ tathaiva ca hṛdayaṃ cintayec cāpi tathā hṛdayabandhanam
english: The teeth, the palate, the tongue, the throat, and likewise the neck; and he should contemplate too the heart, and the heart's binding-cord.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa mayā śiṣyo medhāvī madhusūdana papraccha punar evemaṃ mokṣadharmaṃ sudurvacam
english: Thus addressed by me, that wise disciple, O slayer of Madhu, asked once again about this dharma of liberation, so hard to put into words.

sanskrit: bhuktaṃ bhuktaṃ katham idam annaṃ koṣṭhe vipacyate kathaṃ rasatvaṃ vrajati śoṇitaṃ jāyate katham tathā māṃsaṃ ca medaś ca snāyvasthīni ca poṣati
english: How is this food, once eaten and eaten, digested in the belly? How does it pass into chyle, and how is blood produced? And how does it nourish flesh, and fat, and sinews, and bones?

sanskrit: katham etāni sarvāṇi śarīrāṇi śarīriṇām vardhante vardhamānasya vardhate ca kathaṃ balam nirojasāṃ niṣkramaṇaṃ malānāṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak
english: How do all these bodily parts of embodied beings grow, and how, as one grows, does his strength increase? And how comes the passing out of the spent vital fluids, and of the several impurities, each apart?

sanskrit: kuto vāyaṃ praśvasiti ucchvasity api vā punaḥ kaṃ ca deśam adhiṣṭhāya tiṣṭhaty ātmāyam ātmani
english: From what does this one breathe out, and again breathe in? And, resting upon what place, does this self abide within the self?

sanskrit: jīvaḥ kāyaṃ vahati cec ceṣṭayānaḥ kalevaram kiṃvarṇaṃ kīdṛśaṃ caiva niveśayati vai manaḥ yāthātathyena bhagavan vaktum arhasi me 'nagha
english: If the living soul bears the body, setting the frame in motion, of what color and what manner of being is it that lodges the mind within? Truly, O blessed and sinless one, you are worthy to tell me this.

sanskrit: iti saṃparipṛṣṭo 'haṃ tena vipreṇa mādhava pratyabruvaṃ mahābāho yathāśrutam ariṃdama
english: Thus thoroughly questioned by that brāhmaṇa, O Mādhava, I made answer, O mighty-armed subduer of foes, according to what I had heard.

sanskrit: yathā svakoṣṭhe prakṣipya koṣṭhaṃ bhāṇḍamanā bhavet tathā svakāye prakṣipya mano dvārair aniścalaiḥ ātmānaṃ tatra mārgeta pramādaṃ parivarjayet
english: As a man, having stored away the vessels in his own storeroom, fixes his mind upon that store, so, having cast the mind into his own body through the unwavering gates, one should there seek out the self, shunning all heedlessness.

sanskrit: evaṃ satatam udyuktaḥ prītātmā nacirād iva āsādayati tad brahma yad dṛṣṭvā syāt pradhānavit
english: Thus ever striving, his self made glad, before long he reaches that Brahman, beholding which one becomes the knower of Pradhāna.

sanskrit: na tv asau cakṣuṣā grāhyo na ca sarvair apīndriyaiḥ manasaiva pradīpena mahān ātmani dṛśyate
english: Yet it is not to be grasped by the eye, nor even by all the senses together; by the mind alone, as by a lamp, the Great One is beheld within the self.

sanskrit: sarvataḥpāṇipādaṃ taṃ sarvatokṣiśiromukham jīvo niṣkrāntam ātmānaṃ śarīrāt saṃprapaśyati
english: With hands and feet on every side, with eyes, heads, and faces on every side—the living soul fully beholds that self gone forth out of the body.

sanskrit: sa tad utsṛjya dehaṃ svaṃ dhārayan brahma kevalam ātmānam ālokayati manasā prahasann iva
english: Casting off that body of his and holding fast to Brahman alone, he gazes upon the self with the mind, as it were laughing in joy.

sanskrit: idaṃ sarvarahasyaṃ te mayoktaṃ dvijasattama āpṛcche sādhayiṣyāmi gaccha śiṣya yathāsukham
english: This whole mystery has been declared by me to you, O most excellent of the twice-born. I take my leave and shall depart; go, disciple, as it pleases you.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tadā kṛṣṇa mayā śiṣyo mahātapāḥ agacchata yathākāmaṃ brāhmaṇaś chinnasaṃśayaḥ
english: Thus addressed by me then, O Kṛṣṇa, that disciple of great austerity, the brāhmaṇa, his doubts now severed, departed as he wished.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca ity uktvā sa tadā vākyaṃ māṃ pārtha dvijapuṃgavaḥ mokṣadharmāśritaḥ samyak tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Vāsudeva said: Having spoken these words to me then, O Pārtha, that bull among the twice-born, who had rightly taken his stand upon the dharma of liberation, vanished then and there.

sanskrit: kaccid etat tvayā pārtha śrutam ekāgracetasā tadāpi hi rathasthas tvaṃ śrutavān etad eva hi
english: Have you, O Pārtha, heard this with a single-pointed mind? For even then, standing upon your chariot, you had heard this very thing.

sanskrit: naitat pārtha suvijñeyaṃ vyāmiśreṇeti me matiḥ nareṇākṛtasaṃjñena vidagdhenākṛtātmanā
english: This, O Pārtha, is not easily understood by a man of distracted mind—so I hold—by one whose perception is unformed, who is shallow and whose self is unperfected.

sanskrit: surahasyam idaṃ proktaṃ devānāṃ bharatarṣabha kaccin nedaṃ śrutaṃ pārtha martyenānyena kena cit
english: This great secret of the gods has been declared, O bull of the Bharatas. Surely, O Pārtha, this has not been heard by any other mortal?

sanskrit: na hy etac chrotum arho 'nyo manuṣyas tvām ṛte 'nagha naitad adya suvijñeyaṃ vyāmiśreṇāntarātmanā
english: For no other man than you is worthy to hear this, O sinless one; nor is it now easily understood by one whose inner self is confused.

sanskrit: kriyāvadbhir hi kaunteya devalokaḥ samāvṛtaḥ na caitad iṣṭaṃ devānāṃ martyai rūpanivartanam
english: For by those given to ritual works, O son of Kuntī, the world of the gods is filled; and the gods do not wish this turning back from form to be granted to mortals.

sanskrit: parā hi sā gatiḥ pārtha yat tad brahma sanātanam yatrāmṛtatvaṃ prāpnoti tyaktvā duḥkhaṃ sadā sukhī
english: For that, O Pārtha, is the supreme goal, that which is the eternal Brahman, where one attains immortality and, having cast off sorrow, is happy forever.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi dharmam āsthāya ye 'pi syuḥ pāpayonayaḥ striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrās te 'pi yānti parāṃ gatim
english: For taking their stand thus upon this dharma, even those who may be of base birth—women, vaiśyas, and likewise śūdras—they too attain the supreme goal.
